# OMNI

> OMNI is a deterministic pre-execution trust and risk API for software packages, dependency sets, repositories, and x402 endpoints. It returns advisory assessments with source-attributed evidence; it is not a settlement authority and does not authorize, sign, block, or settle payments.

This document is rendered with the configured public base URL at runtime. Production links resolve to https://api.askomni.xyz.

## Paid API

All four endpoints require x402 payment per request.

Paid calls also require an `Idempotency-Key` header containing a UUID v4. Reuse the same value when retrying one logical request; using it with different validated input returns a conflict. Completed results replay without another payment, and already-paid incomplete requests recover without another payment.

For successful JSON responses, OMNI always returns the canonical structured assessment inline plus an additive Markdown artifact generated deterministically from that same canonical result:

```json
{
  "artifact": {
    "filename": "<fixed service filename>",
    "mediaType": "text/markdown",
    "content": "<markdown>"
  }
}
```

Fixed filenames are `package.risk.md` for `GET /v1/package/risk`, `repo.risk.md` for `GET /v1/repo/risk`, `dependencies.risk.md` for `POST /v1/dependencies/risk`, and `x402.endpoint.preflight.md` for `GET /v1/x402/endpoint/preflight`. No `Accept` header, `Accept: application/json`, and `Accept: */*` return the canonical JSON and artifact payload in the same HTTP 200 response. `Accept: text/markdown` returns only the pure deterministic Markdown representation. Unsupported or zero-quality `Accept` values return HTTP 406 before payment. Successful representations include `Vary: Accept`; switching representation during replay does not execute or settle again. Payment and other error responses remain JSON. Artifact-capable clients may materialize the supplied filename and content; OMNI does not write client files.

- [GET /v1/package/risk](https://omni.example.com/v1/package/risk): package risk assessment ($0.005 USDC). Query: `ecosystem`, `name`, `version`.
- [GET /v1/repo/risk](https://omni.example.com/v1/repo/risk): repository risk assessment ($0.01 USDC). Query: `owner`, `repo`.
- [POST /v1/dependencies/risk](https://omni.example.com/v1/dependencies/risk): per-package assessment for up to 100 packages plus an aggregate summary ($0.05 USDC). Body: `packages[]`.
- [GET /v1/x402/endpoint/preflight](https://omni.example.com/v1/x402/endpoint/preflight): x402 endpoint preflight assessment ($0.01 USDC). Query: `url`.

## Assessment semantics

- `recommendation` is one of `proceed`, `proceed_with_caution`, `manual_review`, `do_not_proceed`. It is advisory output from deterministic policy using observed risk and, where applicable, evidence sufficiency; it is not an authorization decision, and `do_not_proceed` does not prohibit a payment.
- `riskScore` is an integer 0..100 where higher means more observed decision-relevant risk signals. For repository assessments, source failures and coverage loss do not increase the observed `riskScore`; package and x402 assessment scoring remain subject-specific.
- `scoreStatus` is `measured`, `measured_partial`, or `insufficient_evidence` and exposes whether modeled evidence is sufficient for normal recommendation handling. It is an evidence-sufficiency state, not statistical confidence.
- `evidenceCoverage` is the 0..1 fraction of applicable evidence paths expected for that subject type that resolved. It is not statistical confidence or a probability of safety.
- Repository assessments separate observed risk from evidence completeness. GitHub Repository Evidence, OpenSSF Scorecard, Dependency Resolution, OSV Dependency Vulnerabilities, CISA KEV, deps.dev Provenance, and Threat Intelligence are attributed independently. Repository dependency resolution supports exact NPM/Cargo lockfile coordinates, exact `requirements*.txt` pins, authoritative `pyproject.toml` + uv/Poetry lock bindings, and selected Go module coordinates only when proven by a consistent `vendor/modules.txt` snapshot. Bare `go.mod` requirements remain minimum-version evidence and unresolved. Repository OSV scans map proven coordinates to `npm`, `crates.io`, `PyPI`, and `Go`, correlate CVE IDs with CISA KEV, keep `MAL-*` records separate without invented severity, and retain incomplete/deferred results as `UNKNOWN`.
- Repository source failures reduce coverage and can gate the recommendation to `manual_review`, but missing evidence is not itself an observed repository security finding. Repository OSV/KEV findings remain nested in `RepositoryEvidence` and do not populate `RiskSnapshot.vulnerabilities`, but they activate deterministic repository scoring. Vulnerability risk uses the existing severity weights, explicit CISA KEV matches use the repository known-exploitation weight, and the strongest observed repository dimension wins via `MAX` rather than finding-count addition.
- `not_applicable` means a dimension does not apply to that subject; it is distinct from `unknown`, which means relevant evidence has not established the dimension.
- `sourceErrors` lists named upstream sources that failed during the assessment. Treat results with source errors as less complete, not as safe.
- `freshness.expiresAt` is an advisory deadline derived from evidence expiry. Callers should re-run preflight after `expiresAt`; do not silently continue acting on expired evidence.
- Repository Scorecard status may be `available`, `not_indexed`, `unavailable`, or `error`; `not_indexed` means no indexed Scorecard result exists, not that the provider is generally unavailable.
- OSV `MAL-*` records are returned separately as `maliciousPackageObservations`, without invented OSV severity. An active exact-version MAL observation can trigger deterministic malicious-package repository risk; explicitly withdrawn MAL records are not active observations.
- Repository dependency Threat Intelligence is an observed repository risk dimension when an exact licensed match exists. Missing, unavailable, unknown, unresolved, deferred, or partial evidence affects coverage and recommendation gating, not direct observed risk.
- Repository security-practice risk includes Scorecard and observed GitHub findings such as lifecycle scripts, mutable Action refs, workflow write permissions, download/execute patterns, and strong verified provenance mismatches. Counts are evidence detail, not a repository-size penalty.

## x402 endpoint preflight workflow

1. Discover the intended target.
2. Request an OMNI preflight for the target resource URL before your agent calls or pays it.
3. Inspect `recommendation`, `evidenceCoverage`, `signals`, `evidence`, `sourceErrors`, and `freshness`.
4. Obtain the actual HTTP 402 `PaymentRequired` challenge from the target.
5. Compare the selected `PaymentRequirements` from `accepts[]` with OMNI's `preflightContext.paymentOptions` using the local consistency helper.
6. Apply caller/user/runtime wallet policy to the assessment and consistency result.
7. Pay only if local policy allows; the wallet/runtime enforces that decision and Circle performs settlement.

The response includes `preflightContext.resource` and `preflightContext.paymentOptions`: every payment option observed from Circle Discovery (`scheme`, `network`, `amount`, `asset`, `payTo`, and `maxTimeoutSeconds` as observed; absent fields are omitted). Observed Circle Gateway metadata is retained under `extra.name`, `extra.version`, and `extra.verifyingContract` when present.

The consistency model is `preflight observation → actual selected PaymentRequirements / 402 challenge → consistency comparison → match | repreflight_required | insufficient_context → caller policy → wallet enforcement`. A mismatching or stale challenge requires a fresh assessment or caller-side denial before automatic payment.

x402 `PaymentRequirements.amount` is an atomic-unit string. Numeric canonicalization accepts only `^\d+$`; leading zeros may normalize, while decimal fractions and exponent notation never match an integer amount. A `match` means only that the payment requirements match one complete previously observed option. It does NOT mean risk-free, sanctioned-clean, authorized, or guaranteed safe. OMNI does not authorize payment.

## Machine-readable references

- [OpenAPI specification](https://omni.example.com/openapi.yaml)
- [Health check](https://omni.example.com/health) (process liveness only)
- [Readiness](https://omni.example.com/ready) (replica can accept paid requests)

`/v1/repo/audit` and `/v1/audits/{id}` are future roadmap concepts and are not currently available or part of this implemented endpoint list.

## Current paid acceptance

Real Arc Testnet x402 paid lifecycle has been verified on the tested OMNI paid path, including Circle Agent Wallet payment, Gateway settlement, durable PostgreSQL persistence, OMNI execution, recovery/replay, and Circle transfer reconciliation. This is not an exhaustive route-by-route, mainnet, multi-chain, or fleet-capacity claim.
